rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly on this tiny (584-byte text, 3-function) FP-heavy benchmark, so I am raising aggression while respecting that flops/fbench/whetstone-style code spends nearly all its time in tight FP loops where control-flow transforms (BCF, FLA) are the most expensive per-execution. SUB gets the highest weights because arithmetic identity substitution is nearly free at runtime, diversifies the FP/integer instruction mix, and directly obscures the numeric kernels that dominate this program. IBR and ICALL get strong Security/Diversity weights with moderate cost weights to add indirect dispatch and call indirection across the hot loop bodies, while FLA is kept at a solid but not maximal level so flattening is applied where loop structure favors it without payrolling every hot block; BCF is held to the lowest Security weight of the control-flow passes since its runtime and size bloat hurt most in a benchmark binary. SPLIT and IGV are cheap structural/constant-hiding transforms with low risk, so they receive moderate-to-high Diversity weights to fragment basic blocks and conceal global constants (FP tables, format strings) at negligible overhead, and all CorrectnessRisk weights stay low given the clean round-1 run.
